findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed the single-use utensils in the student self-service station were stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The inspector educated about the importance of storing utensils in a manner that prevents students from touching the food contact portions of utensils. The PIC removed the utensils and brought them into the kitchen to correct the storage after lunch. Ensure that single-use articles are stored to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observes the floor behind the cooking equipment, especially behind and to the right of the oven, to be soiled with what appears to be rodent droppings. The staff states that they have not seen rodents. Ensure that the individuals responsible for cleaning the floor clean this area thoroughly. Clean and maintain clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed mouse droppings around and behind the oven, especially along the wall and in the corner near the piping. Person-in-charge states that mice have been observed and a large amount of droppings are swept up regularly. District is responsible for providing pest-control services to the school. Ensure that 3rd-party pest control is sufficient to prevent rodents from entering the facility. No apparent harborage conditions exist. Facility is generally clean with no accumulation of food or other residue/debris. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed x3 cans in the dry storage room which were sharply dented on the top seams. These cans were immediately removed by operator during the inspection. All other cans are in good condition. Ensure that all cans coming into the facility are in good condition on arrival to prevent contaminated/adulterated foods from being used in food preparation. Corrected on site. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The vinyl trim at the bottom corner of the wall between the refrigerator/freezer section and the main kitchen next to the hand sink is beginning to peel away from the wall leaving an area of wall exposed and difficult to clean. Operator was shown corner at the time of inspection. Ensure that this trim has been repaired and that the surface is smooth, durable, non-absorbent and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The triple sink in the kitchen was observed to be missing caulking along the right wall of the sink where the metal has pulled away from the wall. Ensure caulking is placed in this gap to allow for easy cleaning of a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
